## Findings
- claim-1: From the accepted integral interval/Pieri presentation, the requested target is established for \(p=c=1\) and \(0\le k\le b:=\min(i,j)\): \(M_{d+k}\) has basis \(P_{x,k-x}\) \((0\le x\le k)\), and all positive-degree multiplication relations in degree \(d+k\) are exactly \(\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1})\), where \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\).
## Strategy
Under the accepted interval/Schur/Pieri presentation, the argument proves the stated result for
\[
0\le k\le b:=\min(i,j).
\]
Writing \(C_x=P_{x,k-x}\), the interval Schur basis is
\[
M_{d+k}=\bigoplus_{x=0}^{k}\mathbb ZC_x.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=\sum_{t=1}^{k}h_tM_{d+k-t},
\]
since \(A_+=(h_1,h_2,\ldots)\) and \(M_{<d}=0\). For every admissible row index \(0\le x\le k-t\), interval Pieri gives
\[
h_tP_{x,k-t-x}=C_x+C_{x+1}.
\]
Thus every positive-degree multiplication row lies in
\[
L_k:=\sum_{x=0}^{k-1}\mathbb Z(C_x+C_{x+1}).
\]
Conversely the \(t=1\) rows are exactly \(C_x+C_{x+1}\) for \(0\le x<k\), so
\[
(A_+M)_{d+k}=L_k.
\]
For \(k=0\), this subgroup is zero.

## Gaps
The requested target is established only in the bounded range \(0\le k\le b\), conditional on the accepted integral interval/Pieri presentation. The literal assertion for every degree \(d+k\), including \(k>b\), is not established by the supplied presentation: the displayed interval basis and two-term Pieri classification were proved only in that range.

## Next
For a literal all-degree statement, classify the interval partitions and complete Pieri row lattices for \(k>b\), including boundary one-term rows, and prove the corresponding equality with \((A_+M)_{d+k}\).
